## Historical audit — S0271

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/results/task02/reference/H_start/selection/commons_92056365/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; supplied observations are whole lines, not split fragments.

| Stage | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student was asked to reconstruct a 512 × 379 indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, colors, proportions and occlusions. The student’s *inferred* scene inventory described a cafeteria with glazing, booths, tables, chairs, pendants and plants; this audit cannot independently inspect the photograph (lines 1, 3). |
| First build | The student emitted a complete program with multiple named object assemblies and child parts: furniture seats, backs and pedestals; lamp shades and wires; palm trunk, fronds and leaflets. The code used colored surfaces and roughness/metallic settings, rather than an explicit image texture; physical part connection and reference fidelity were not independently checked. It set a camera and three area lights (lines 3–4). |
| Validation and revision | Step 1 executed successfully in 42.3 seconds, saved a render and blend file, and was selected (lines 5–6). The next request supplied the reference and first render to the student (lines 7–8). The student reported too little right glazing, an out-of-frame palm, low rear ceiling and overly light upholstery. These are student observations, not independently verified defects. The revised program changed camera aim, furniture and lamp placement, palm position and detail, colors and lighting; step 2 was actually executed (lines 9–10). |
| Outcome | Step 2 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file in 52.9 seconds, and was selected (lines 11–12). This is **technical execution success**, not established visual or geometric success. No final comparison, score, or post-step-2 student review is visible; overall reconstruction correctness remains unknown. No empty patch, algorithm failure or technical interruption is shown. |
| Input and autonomy | No teacher message, teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-advised execution appears in this student trace; consequently teacher receipt or adoption cannot be established. The render-comparison prompt and image were runner feedback, not identified teacher input. Both recorded student sessions had zero tool calls; the build–render–revise loop is visible, but separate autonomous exploration is not (lines 2, 7–8). |

**Scene uncertainty and lessons.** Multiple objects, materials, intended part relationships and camera/light settings are evidenced by code, not verified against either image. Chair facing and palm-frond orientations are parameterized, but their correct pose, actual connections, texture appearance, and final camera, lighting or render defects remain unknown. A transferable observation is that a successful render enabled a targeted revision; it does not prove the revision improved the match. The glazing, palm and upholstery diagnoses are task-specific hypotheses, and their resolution is unverified.
